paragraphs.text:
The greening of planes, trains and automobiles

Moving goods and people around the world is responsible for a large part of global CO2 emissions (排放). As the world races to decarbonize everything, it faces particular problems with transportation — which accounts for about a quarter of our energy-related greenhouse gas emissions. Here’s the breakdown of the emissions in 2018 for different modes of transport.

ROAD VEHICLES
ROAD (PASSENGER) 45.1%
ROAD (GOODS) 29.4%
AIRPLANES 11.6%
SHIPPING 10.6%
RAIL 1%
OTHER 2.2%

The fuels for transport need to be not just green, cheap and powerful, but also lightweight and safe enough to be carried around. Each mode of transport has its specific fuel needs. Much is still to be settled, but here are some of the solutions to get us going green. PLANES — Synthetic hydrocarbons. The hardest sector to decarbonize is aviation. One long-term option for sustainable fuel for planes is to make hydrocarbons from recycled air. CARS — Batteries. Batteries are energy-efficient and electric cars can plug into existing systems and services. New solid-state batteries will take a car farther on a single charge. TRAINS — Electricity. Some trains are already electrified through rails or wires; others can be made electric in pretty simple ways. TRUCKS — Hydrogen fuel cells. Hydrogen fuel cells are a lighter choice than batteries for trucks, but making green hydrogen is expensive. SHIPS — Liquid ammonia. Liquid ammonia is easy to keep and transport, but it is hard to ignite (点燃) and requires an engine redesign.

This energy transition (变革) is global, and the amount of renewable energy the world will need is “a little bit mind-blowing,” says mechanical engineer Keith Wipke at the National Renewable Energy Laboratory. It’s estimated that the global demand for electricity could more than double by 2050. Fortunately, analyses suggest that renewables are up to the task. “We need to speed up the development of green energy, and it will all get used,” says Wipke.

In my ninth-grade writing class last year, I met a cowboy who saved his town, a strict father who demanded his son earn straight A’s, and a modern-day Juliet who died of heartbreak after her parents rejected the love of her young life. More than once, I found myself wondering just how my students, who’d created these people, knew their subjects so well.

But things were different for their first essay, which was about the question: “Why is writing important?” Most of the essays filled less than one page, and few contained a sentence that could be interpreted as a thesis (论点) statement. I was shocked. Then I realized that the problem was the question itself. They could have written pages on the necessity of computers, but writing, in and of itself, simply didn’t strike them as important. This would have to change.

As a new unit started, I asked everyone to write a persuasive piece on a health-related topic of their choice. This time they found the exercise much more interesting. For the next two assignments, a personal-narrative unit followed by a creative-writing workshop, I only required that the piece meet the specifications of its genre (体裁) and that it contain a thesis. The results were staggering. The students took on diverse topics and turned in stories, 10 to 20 pages each, with characters that broadened my view and touched my heart.

I walked into class believing that writing is important as a means of communication. However, my students demonstrated something more important to me. When the final bell rang in June, I walked away with a yearbook full of messages about writing’s most powerful significance — the ability to connect people, to put us in another’s skin, to teach us what it means to be human.

While safety improvements might have been made to our streets in recent years, transport studies also show declines in pedestrian (行人) mobility, especially among young children. Many parents say there’s too much traffic on the roads for their children to walk safely to school, so they pack them into the car instead. Dutch authors Thalia Verkade and Marco te Brömmelstroet are bothered by facts like these. In their new book Movement: How to Take Back Our Streets and Transform Our Lives, they call for a rethink of our streets and the role they play in our lives.

Life on city streets started to change decades ago. Whole neighbourhoods were destroyed to make way for new road networks and kids had to play elsewhere. Some communities fought back. Most famously, a Canadian journalist who had moved her family to Manhattan in the early 1950s led a campaign to stop the destruction of her local park. Describing her alarm at its proposed replacement with an expressway, Jane Jacobs called on her mayor (市长) to champion “New York as a decent place to live, and not just rush through.” Similar campaigns occurred in Australia in the late 1960s and 1970s as well.

Although these campaigns were widespread, the reality is that the majority of the western cities were completely redesigned around the needs of the motor car. The number of cars on roads has been increasing rapidly. In Australia we now have over twenty million cars for just over twenty-six million people, among the highest rate of car ownership in the world.

We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs. Do we really recognise what it costs us as a society when children can’t move safely around our communities? The authors of Movement have it right: it’s time to think differently about that street outside your front door.

Microplastics have become a common source of pollution across the Earth — they have settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas, stuck inside volcanic rocks, filled the stomachs of seabirds and even fallen in fresh Antarctic snow. They are even appearing inside humans.

Now, new research suggests that a simple, cheap measure may significantly reduce the level of microplastics in water from your tap (水龙头): boiling and filtering (过滤) it. In a study published Wednesday in Environmental Science & Technology Letters, researchers from China found that boiling tap water for just five minutes — then filtering it after it cools — could remove at least 80 percent of its microplastics.

Crucially, this process relies on the water containing enough calcium carbonate (碳酸钙) to trap the plastics. In the study, boiling hard water containing 300 milligrams of calcium carbonate led to an almost 90 percent drop in plastics. But in samples with less than 60 milligrams of calcium carbonate, boiling reduced the level of plastics by just 25 percent. Additionally, the research didn’t include all types of plastics. The team focused only on three common types — polystyrene, polyethylene and polypropylene — and they didn’t study other chemicals previously found in water such as vinyl chloride.

Still, the findings show a potential path forward for reducing microplastic exposure — a task that’s becoming increasingly difficult. Even bottled water, scientists found earlier this year, contains 10 to 1,000 times more microplastics than originally thought.

Scientists are still trying to determine how harmful microplastics are — but what they do know has raised concerns. The new study suggests boiling tap water could be a tool to limit intake. “The way they demonstrated how microplastics were trapped through the boiling process was nice,” Caroline Gauchette-Lindsay, an environmental engineer of the University of Glasgow in Scotland who was not involved in the research, tells New Scientist. “We should be looking into upgrading drinking water treatment plants so they remove microplastics.”

items.promptZh: 2018 年全球交通排放中，道路交通工具占多少？

explanation.summaryZh: 道路客运占 45.1%，道路货运占 29.4%，合计为 74.5%。
explanation.ruleZh: 图表题先识别题干对象，再合并同一大类下的分项数据。

distractors.reasonZh: 11.6% 是飞机排放占比。
45.1% 只是道路客运这一分项。
86.1% 不是图表中道路交通工具的合计值。

items.promptZh: Which mode of transport can go green comparatively easily?

explanation.summaryZh: 原文指出，有些火车已经电气化，其他火车也可以用比较简单的方式实现电动化。
explanation.ruleZh: 细节题要回到原文定位比较级或程度副词对应的句子。

evidence.quote: others can be made electric in pretty simple ways

distractors.reasonZh: 飞机是最难脱碳的领域。
卡车的绿色氢能制造成本高。
船舶需要重新设计发动机。

items.promptZh: What does Wipke suggest regarding energy transition?

explanation.summaryZh: Wipke 的建议是加快绿色能源的发展，因为未来的需求会继续增长。
explanation.ruleZh: 人物观点题优先寻找引号中的直接引语，再判断选项是否准确概括建议。

evidence.quote: We need to speed up the development of green energy

distractors.reasonZh: 原文没有建议限制燃料消耗。
原文强调发展绿色能源，而不是泛泛提高能源效率。
原文没有提出降低电价。

items.promptZh: Who are the people mentioned at the beginning of paragraph 1?

explanation.summaryZh: 段首列举的是学生创作出来的牛仔、严厉的父亲和现代版朱丽叶，都是虚构人物。
explanation.ruleZh: 人物指代题要区分故事中的角色和现实中的作者、学生。

evidence.quote: my students, who’d created these people

distractors.reasonZh: 学生是这些人物的创作者，不是题干所指的人物。
段首没有介绍学生家长。
段首人物来自学生作文，不是现实作家。

items.promptZh: Why did the students perform poorly in writing their first essay?

explanation.summaryZh: 教师后来意识到，学生表现差是因为“为什么写作重要”这个题目本身没有激发他们的兴趣。
explanation.ruleZh: 因果题要把结果句与后文的转折、解释句连起来，不能只根据前文猜测。

evidence.quote: the problem was the question itself

distractors.reasonZh: 原文没有说时间不够。
原文没有把问题归因于词汇量。
学生并非误解题目，而是认为写作本身不重要。

options.text: They were not given enough time.
They had a very limited vocabulary.
They had little interest in the topic.

items.promptZh: What does the underlined word “staggering” in paragraph 3 mean?

explanation.summaryZh: 后文列出学生写出 10 到 20 页、主题多样且打动人心的作品，因此 staggering 表示令人惊叹的。
explanation.ruleZh: 词义猜测题要用词语所在句的上下文结果和评价色彩判断。

distractors.reasonZh: 作品结果不是“混杂的”。
学生作品并非相似，而是主题多样。
上下文表达的是积极惊喜，不是令人不安。

items.promptZh: What does the author’s experience show?

explanation.summaryZh: 教师通过教学经历也发现了新的认识，说明教学过程同时也是学习过程。
explanation.ruleZh: 主旨概括题要综合首尾和转折后的核心认识，不能只看学生作品数量。

evidence.quote: my students demonstrated something more important to me

distractors.reasonZh: 文章没有讨论停滞不前。
文章重点不是知识的力量。
练习有帮助，但不是作者在结尾强调的认识。

items.promptZh: What phenomenon does the author point out in paragraph 1?

explanation.summaryZh: 文章指出，儿童步行活动减少，家长因为交通拥挤而更多选择开车送孩子。
explanation.ruleZh: 段落细节题要同时关注研究结论和后面的具体解释。

distractors.reasonZh: 段落没有说汽车经常堵在路上。
段落谈到交通压力，但没有指出事故频繁。
问题不在于行人不遵守规则，而在于步行空间和交通环境。

options.text: Cars often get stuck on the road.
People walk less and drive more.
Pedestrians fail to follow the rules.

items.promptZh: What were the Canadian journalist and other campaigners trying to do?

explanation.summaryZh: 他们反对为了道路建设破坏社区空间，目标是让城市适合生活，而不只是方便汽车快速通过。
explanation.ruleZh: 推断题要把人物行动与引用中的价值判断合并理解。

evidence.quote: New York as a decent place to live, and not just rush through

distractors.reasonZh: 文章没有把活动目标归结为文化多样性。
活动并非为帮助贫困家庭。
他们反对用高速路替代公园，而不是推动高速路建设。

items.promptZh: What can be inferred about the campaigns in Australia in the late 1960s and 1970s?

explanation.summaryZh: 尽管澳大利亚也出现了类似活动，但城市后来仍围绕汽车重新设计，说明这些活动总体效果有限。
explanation.ruleZh: 推断题要结合 although 引出的让步关系和后文现实结果。

evidence.quote: the majority of the western cities were completely redesigned around the needs of the motor car

distractors.reasonZh: 活动并未促进汽车销售。
文章没有说活动获得政府支持。
活动目标是保护适宜生活的城市空间，而不是建设新公园。

options.text: They boosted the sales of cars.

items.promptZh: What can be a suitable title for the text?

explanation.summaryZh: 文章批评城市一味追求快速通行，呼吁重新思考街道和城市生活，因此标题是“为什么如此匆忙”。
explanation.ruleZh: 标题题要概括全文问题和作者态度，而不是只对应某个例子。

evidence.quote: it’s time to think differently about that street outside your front door

distractors.reasonZh: 文章不是在预测未来安排。
文章没有讨论居住地点选择。
文章重点是城市规划和生活方式，不是在追责。

items.promptZh: How does the author present the issue in the first paragraph?

explanation.summaryZh: 第一段列举微塑料出现在深海、喜鸟胃部和南极雪等多个地点的事实，以统计和事实数据呈现问题。
explanation.ruleZh: 篇章手法题要看段落如何组织信息，多个地点和范围数据体现的是事实列举与数据呈现。

evidence.quote: settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas

distractors.reasonZh: 第一段没有引用专家观点。
第一段没有给出概念定义。
列举的是微塑料出现的位置和事实，不是具体案例故事。

items.promptZh: What determines the effectiveness of trapping microplastics in water?

explanation.summaryZh: 研究结果显示，水的硬度及其中碳酸钙含量会影响煮沸捕获微塑料的效果。
explanation.ruleZh: 细节题要根据实验条件和结果寻找决定效果的变量。

evidence.quote: boiling hard water containing 300 milligrams of calcium carbonate

distractors.reasonZh: 原文没有把冷却时间作为决定因素。
过滤次数没有在研究中作为变量讨论。
研究限定了部分塑料类型，但题目问的是捕获效果的决定因素。

options.text: The type of plastic in water.

items.promptZh: What does the author try to illustrate by mentioning bottled water in paragraph 4?

explanation.summaryZh: 瓶装水中的微塑料含量也远高于原先估计，进一步说明微塑料污染问题的严重性。
explanation.ruleZh: 例证作用题要看例子支持了哪一个上位观点。

evidence.quote: contains 10 to 1,000 times more microplastics than originally thought

distractors.reasonZh: 段落没有讨论塑料回收。
文章没有说过度饮用纯净水是危险。
例子强调污染范围和严重程度，而非具体处理难度。

options.text: The severity of the microplastic problem.
The danger in overusing pure water.
The difficulty in treating polluted water.

items.promptZh: What is Gauchette-Lindsay’s suggestion about?

explanation.summaryZh: 她建议升级饮用水处理厂，使其能够去除微塑料，这是研究发现的潜在应用方向。
explanation.ruleZh: 人物观点题要定位直接引语，并区分研究方法、后续研究和实际应用。

evidence.quote: upgrading drinking water treatment plants so they remove microplastics

distractors.reasonZh: 她没有建议更换研究方法。
她提出的是处理设施的应用改进，不是抽象的后续研究方向。
她没有要求增加研究人员。

items.promptZh: 阅读下面短文，从短文后的选项中选出可以填入空白处的最佳选项。选项中有两项为多余选项。

explanation.summaryZh: 五个空分别考查总起句、动作顺序、事实补充、人物感受和结尾照应。
explanation.ruleZh: 七选五先看段落功能，再利用代词、时间顺序、语义复现和首尾照应确定选项。

sharedOptions.text: The cafe closes at 9 pm every day.
She has two children aged eight and four.
Sometimes she arrives early to serve the students early.
After finishing an order, she calls out the name on the cup.
Not only does this cafe serve up drinks, it also serves up smiles.
Going to the cafe starts her day off good and gets her ready for class.
She has served here for 17 years and can’t imagine working anywhere else.

segments.text:
An Unsung Hero

Need a break between classes or just a quick pick-me-up in the morning? The College Cafe has just that, and more.
Catherine Murphy, a cafe worker in a green shirt and black hat, makes sure that each customer gets exactly what they order. She goes back and forth between machines to make the drinks.

As the customer grabs the drink from her hand, she smiles and says, “Hello, how is your day?” Even when the line is getting longer, she doesn’t let it get in the way of her genuine conversations.

Murphy gets up at a quarter to five and drives thirty minutes every day to get to work on time.

“I do so because I like to make coffee for the students. I know they need it in the morning,” Murphy said. Being a mother and wife has helped her become the woman she is. She believes she is here to serve.

One thing Murphy may not know is that her smile is contagious (有感染力) and can be the difference in a student having a much better day than they were having before seeing her. Joanna Wright, a senior political science major, loves coffee and goes to the cafe at least six days a week.

“Catherine always has a huge smile on her face, which always puts me in a cheerful mood,” Wright said.

“I enjoy working in the cafe,” Murphy said.
She has every intention of staying and continuing doing what she loves.

gaps.explanationZh: 开头总起句说明咖啡馆不仅提供饮品，也带来笑容，与后文服务员的微笑照应。
先完成订单，再叫顾客名字，随后顾客从她手中接过饮料，符合动作顺序。
前文写她很早起床并准时到岗，补充她早到为学生服务最连贯。
后文 Wright 说她的笑容让自己心情愉快，前句应是去咖啡馆让她以好状态开始一天。
后句说明她打算继续留下，前句补充她已在这里工作 17 年并不愿离开。

items.promptZh: 阅读下面短文，从每题所给的 A、B、C、D 四个选项中选出最佳选项。

explanation.summaryZh: 文章讲述搬家时通过网络赠送旧花瓶和其他物品，在整理生活的过程中减少浪费并获得人与人之间的联系。
explanation.ruleZh: 完形填空要结合句内搭配、上下文逻辑、词义辨析和全文情感线索逐空判断。

gaps.explanationZh: 搬家前正在清空住了 23 年的房子，emptying out 表示清空。
后文明确说 I sit in my apartment，搬去的是公寓。

买家想要花瓶的更多照片。
搬家日期临近，move day 指搬家日。

与来访者的交流成为混乱生活中的光亮，visits 与 received 搭配。

items.promptZh: 阅读下面短文，在空白处填入 1 个适当的单词或括号内单词的正确形式。

explanation.summaryZh: 语篇介绍围棋展览，考查关系代词、冠词、非谓语、名词、被动语态、主谓一致、介词、形容词、副词和并列连词。
explanation.ruleZh: 语法填空先判断句子成分，再根据固定搭配、语态、时态、词性和上下文完成形式变化。

segments.text: An exhibition at the Jiushi Art Museum in Shanghai is featuring artwork inspired by Go, or weiqi in Chinese,

originated in China more than 4,000 years ago.

Go is one of

earliest binary-based (基于二元的) games. The movements of the black and white pieces reflect the basic ideas of Eastern philosophy, according to Tu Ningning, who is in charge of the exhibition.

“The exhibition brings together Go culture, cutting-edge technology and contemporary art,” says Tu. “We hope

(present) the rather abstract Go game and AI in a visual context, and initiate dialogues with minimalist art, conceptual art and expressionism.”

“In a Go game, each move should serve a long-term goal. You try to lead the opponent into your trap and force them to follow your

(guide) till they lose,” explains Wang Wei, a Go player among the visitors to the exhibition.

“The players’ personalities
(reveal) during the game, and one’s weaknesses are exposed to the opponent,” she adds. “A decent winner always
(try) to beat the opponent

no more than one or two points as a gesture (姿态) of respect for the other side.”

Tu says that the balance between the black and white pieces, the beauty in the
(strategy) placement of the pieces,
the energy flow following each move inspired artists to create oil paintings, sculptures,
(digital) generated pictures and silk-screen prints for the exhibition.

gaps.explanationZh: 非限制性定语从句修饰 Go，使用关系代词 which。
one of the + 形容词最高级/序数意义短语，使用定冠词 the。
hope 后接不定式作宾语，present 使用 to present。
your 后需要名词，guide 变为 guidance。
personalities 与 reveal 构成被动关系，且主语为复数，使用 are revealed。
主语 a decent winner 为第三人称单数，一般现在时使用 tries。
by no more than 表示不超过，使用介词 by。
placement 前需要形容词，strategy 变为 strategic。
the balance、the beauty 和 the energy flow 是并列成分，使用 and。

items.promptZh: 假定你是李华，你班的英语报要增设一个栏目。外教 Jenny 提出“Fun at my school”和“Guess who I am”两个选项供大家选择。请给 Jenny 写一封邮件，内容包括：(1)你的选择；(2)说明理由。注意：写作词数应为 80 个左右，请按题目格式作答。

explanation.summaryZh: 应用文需要明确选择一个栏目，并从增进同学了解、促进友谊和班级氛围等方面说明理由。
explanation.ruleZh: 应用文先完成任务要点，再使用称呼、正文、落款等基本格式组织表达。

openingSentences: I really like the idea of adding a new column to our English newspaper.
items.modelAnswer:
Dear Jenny,

I really like the idea of adding a new column to our English newspaper. I’m writing to express that my predilection goes to “Guess who I am”, which capitalizes on an object clause to signal its potential contents.

The column will serve as a catalyst for closer bonds between students. Redoubling efforts to boost academic performance, we pay little heed to other classmates’ personalities, hobbies, strengths, and even aspirations. Such an inviting column, adopting a “description and guess” approach, must expose everyone to others’ characteristics, thus strengthening mutual understanding. More importantly, more friendships will be forged, since the column enables us to befriend someone on the same wavelength.

This eye-catching column, I’m firmly convinced, won’t fail to grant the whole class a harmonious atmosphere.

Yours,
Li Hua

items.promptZh: 阅读下面材料，根据其内容和所给段落开头语续写两段，使之构成一篇完整的短文。续写词数为 150 个左右。

explanation.summaryZh: 续写围绕兄弟因 Toby 产生矛盾后的和解展开，需要承接愧疚、道歉、见面和重新建立联系的情节。
explanation.ruleZh: 读后续写要承接原文冲突，围绕两个段首句推进动作、对话和情感变化，并保持人物与时态一致。

requirementsZh: 围绕兄弟和解推进情节
openingSentences: I realized it was me who was at fault.
With the biscuits my wife had made, I arrived at my brother’s door.
items.modelAnswer:
I realized it was me who was at fault. I had been so focused on keeping the party under control that I failed to consider how important Toby was to my brother during this difficult time. My pride had kept me from reaching out, and now months had passed without a proper conversation. One evening, I picked up the phone and left him a voice message, apologizing for my behavior and asking if we could meet. To my relief, he called back the next day, and we agreed to get together soon.

With the biscuits my wife had made, I arrived at my brother’s door. He opened it with a surprised smile, and for a moment, neither of us spoke. Then we hugged — something we hadn’t done since before his wife passed away. We sat on the porch with Toby resting beside us, and I handed him the box of biscuits. “Thank you,” he said quietly. We talked for hours, laughing, remembering old times, and slowly rebuilding what had been lost. As I watched Toby gently rest his head on my brother’s leg, I knew we were finally on the path to healing.
